The Bengaluru-headquartered startup raised $26 million in equity funding led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Finserv Intelligence (through Bajaj Finance), Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, Jump Trading LLC and angel investor Anita Pramoda, former CFO of Epic.

The $21 million venture debt round was led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital.

Founded in February 2026 by Manish Agarwal and Ishank Gupta, Humyn Labs prepares physical AI systems for real-world deployment by translating human experience into physical understanding for robots. The startup's proprietary capture devices record how people perform specific tasks across factories, warehouses, farms and homes. Its end-to-end data engine then converts these recordings into labelled, training-ready datasets with verified provenance across sight, sound, motion and touch.

Humyn Labs will use the funds across three areas: building deployment-readiness infrastructure in Brazil, South Korea and India; and expanding its R&D and market presence in San Francisco, London and Seoul.

“Physical AI will only be as good as the real-world data it learns from. This funding will help us strengthen our research, build trust with labs and enterprises, and expand our global presence. With a $10 billion opportunity emerging in data infrastructure, we aim to build a $1 billion annual revenue business and establish ourselves as a global leader in the space,” said Manish Agarwal, Co-founder, Humyn Labs.

According to Humyn Labs, it has surpassed $50 million in annualised revenue within six months of operations. It works with frontier AI labs, robotics companies and world-model developers, and runs its own capture and enrichment operations across 20+ countries in Latin America, East Asia, and South and Southeast Asia.

“A robot does not learn a job from the internet. It learns it from the person who has done it for twenty years, on the floor where it will be done. We bring the model lab and the site operator onto that floor together, so every deployment teaches the next model, and the world’s factories, farms and warehouses become the training se,” said Ishank Gupta, Co-founder, Humyn Labs.

item.title: Disseqt AI raises $8M to build enterprise AI safeguards
item.description: The funds will support the expansion of Disseqt’s enterprise customer base globally. The company is also hiring in India across sales, operations and technology, with plans to expand into London.
item.content:encoded:
Disseqt AI, a Dublin-headquartered AI assurance company with a significant presence in India, has raised $8 million in a round led by Gresham House Ventures, the growth equity arm of investment manager Gresham House. 

Other investors include Sure Valley Ventures, an AI-focused venture fund; Delta Partners, an Irish early-stage investor; and Enterprise Ireland, the Irish government’s enterprise development agency. Angel backers include senior leaders from OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce and Meta, alongside cricket legend Rahul Dravid, who invested in his individual capacity.

The funds will support the expansion of Disseqt’s enterprise customer base globally. The company is also hiring in India across sales, operations and technology, with plans to expand into London.

Disseqt helps organisations test and oversee AI agents, software systems that can take actions, access company data and work across business applications. Its platform tests systems before launch, enforces company policies once they are live, monitors behaviour, blocks outputs that breach rules and maintains audit records.

“Every enterprise is handing real work to AI agents, but very few can prove those agents are safe, fair and within policy,” said Apoorva Kumar, chief executive and co-founder. 

Disseqt claims it improved the safe-response rate of a global sports league’s fan-engagement agent, used by 80 million fans, from 80% to 99% in tests covering safety, bias and privacy.

Founded in late 2025 by Kumar, Manish Atri and Cyril Treacy, whose backgrounds include senior roles at Microsoft, AWS and Salesforce, Disseqt is entering a market where businesses are increasingly moving from AI chatbots to agents capable of performing tasks within company systems.

McKinsey’s 2026 survey found that 40% of respondents at companies with annual revenue exceeding $1 billion were scaling AI agents in at least one business function, compared with 27% a year earlier. 

The risks associated with their deployment are also becoming clearer. OpenAI disclosed in October that two internal coding agents had weakened monitoring safeguards during separate tasks. 

Gresham House Ventures partner Rohit Mathur said companies needed “tools that sit apart from the model providers they rely on”.

Investment is also reaching adjacent areas of the sector. Bengaluru-based Karta AI raised $3 million in October to develop voice agents for financial services, while AI infrastructure company Simplismart secured $14 million in a Series B round to expand its technology for running AI models more efficiently.

item.title: Anthropic raises $81.3B in IPO, surpasses SpaceX's record offering
item.description: Anthropic's IPO surpasses SpaceX's $75 billion offering. The company reported $16.2 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026, up from $1.16 billion in the same period last year, even as its reported net loss widened.
item.content:encoded:
Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic has raised $81.3 billion through its initial public offering (IPO), making it the largest stock market offering on record and surpassing Elon Musk-led space company SpaceX's $75 billion IPO.

Anthropic priced its shares at $83 apiece, above the previously indicated range of $70-78 per share. The company is set to make its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, November 19, at a valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion.

According to the company's statement, the offering comprised 980 million shares, including 956.4 million shares sold by Anthropic and 23.6 million shares sold by its seven co-founders. The founders' share sale is worth approximately $1.96 billion.

Anthropic's IPO will serve as a litmus test for AI companies, with its stock market debut offering an indication of investor appetite for the sector.

The company is also raising $26 billion through a separate private placement, taking the combined value of the IPO and private placement to $107.3 billion.

Co-founded by Dario Amodei and others in 2021, Anthropic reported revenue of $16.29 billion in the first half of 2026, while its net loss widened to $80.75 billion, according to its regulatory filing. In comparison, the company reported revenue of $1.16 billion and a net loss of $12.97 billion in the first half of 2025.

Anthropic’s growth has been remarkable, with annual revenue rising from $41 million in 2023 to $4.59 billion in 2025.

In its IPO filing, Anthropic said, “We believe that AI is one of the most consequential technologies in human history. If managed well, it could rapidly accelerate scientific innovation, greatly increase economic growth rates, bring cures for major diseases within reach and solve problems that have resisted generations of human efforts.”

“Anthropic aims to realise these while navigating and preventing the risks that come with a technological revolution this fast and this powerful.”

Edited by Megha Reddy

item.title: Inside MS Dhoni’s startup playbook: 13 companies backed by Captain Cool
item.description: From Garuda Aerospace to SolarSquare, explore 13 startups backed by MS Dhoni across fintech, electric mobility, gaming and clean energy.
item.content:encoded:
MS Dhoni's retirement from the Indian Premier League (IPL) as a player marks the end of an important chapter in his cricketing career. On November 17, 2026, Chennai Super Kings (CSK) announced that Dhoni would take up the role of team mentor from the 2027 season.

However, cricket is not the only field where Dhoni has built a presence. Over the years, the former Indian captain has invested in several Indian startups through personal investments and his family office, Midas Deals.

His investment portfolio spans fintech, drone technology, electric mobility, food, gaming, digital entertainment and renewable energy.

Here are 13 startups and companies backed by MS Dhoni.

1. Garuda Aerospace

Founded in 2015 by Agnishwar Jayaprakash, Chennai-based Garuda Aerospace develops drones for agriculture, defence, infrastructure and industrial applications. Dhoni invested in the company in June 2022 and became its brand ambassador. In February 2024, he acquired a 1.1% stake for Rs 4 crore.

2. Khatabook

Founded in 2018, Bengaluru-based Khatabook is a fintech platform that helps small businesses and merchants manage digital bookkeeping and daily transactions. Dhoni invested in the startup in March 2020 and also became its brand ambassador. The investment amount was not disclosed.

3. CARS24

CARS24 is a Gurugram-based online marketplace for buying and selling pre-owned vehicles. Founded in 2015, the company uses technology to simplify vehicle valuation, inspection and transactions. Dhoni invested in the startup in August 2019 as part of its Series D funding round.

4. HomeLane

Founded in 2014, HomeLane is a Bengaluru-based home interior design company that helps homeowners plan and customise their living spaces. Its services include modular kitchens, wardrobes and complete home interiors. Dhoni invested in the company in August 2021, although the investment amount was not disclosed.

5. EMotorad

Pune-based EMotorad manufactures electric bicycles for urban commuting and recreational use. Founded in 2020, the company aims to make electric mobility more accessible. Dhoni invested an undisclosed amount in the startup in April 2024 in exchange for equity and also became its brand ambassador.

6. Shaka Harry

Shaka Harry is a plant-based protein and alternative meat brand based in Bengaluru. It develops plant-based food products for consumers looking for alternatives to conventional meat. Dhoni invested in the company in 2022, although the financial details of the investment were not disclosed.

7. 7InkBrews

Mumbai-based 7InkBrews operates in the food and beverage industry. Dhoni became a co-founder, shareholder and brand ambassador of the company in April 2021. Its consumer brand, Copter7, offers chocolates and beverages inspired by Dhoni's iconic helicopter shot and jersey number seven.

8. Tagda Raho

Tagda Raho is a fitness startup that combines traditional Indian exercise techniques with modern fitness practices. Based in Bengaluru, the company promotes indigenous workout methods and fitness equipment. Dhoni invested in the startup in November 2023.

9. ACKO

ACKO is a digital-first insurance company offering products across motor, health and travel insurance. The company uses technology to simplify insurance purchases and claims. In July 2025, Dhoni joined ACKO as an investor and brand ambassador through his family office.

10. Kuku

Kuku is a Bengaluru-based digital storytelling platform operating across audio entertainment, educational content and short-form video. Its products include Kuku FM, Kuku TV and Guru. In March 2026, Dhoni invested in the company and became the brand ambassador for its microdrama platform, Kuku TV. The investment amount was not disclosed.

11. LightFury Games

LightFury Games is a gaming startup developing cricket-based gaming experiences for digital audiences. In 2025, the company raised $11 million in a funding round involving investors such as Blume Ventures, V3 Ventures, MIXI and Times Internet. Dhoni participated as a strategic investor alongside cricketers Jasprit Bumrah, Hardik Pandya and Ravindra Jadeja.

12. SolarSquare

SolarSquare is a rooftop solar company that provides residential solar installation and related services. Founded in 2015, the company helps households adopt solar energy solutions. In July 2026, Dhoni invested in the startup through his family office, Midas Deals, and joined as its brand ambassador as part of its $53 million Series C funding round.

13. BluSmart

BluSmart was an electric mobility startup that operated an all-electric ride-hailing service and EV charging infrastructure. Dhoni's family office invested in the company during its pre-Series B funding round in June 2024. However, the company suspended its ride-hailing operations in 2025 following financial and regulatory challenges.

Final thoughts

MS Dhoni's investments reflect his growing involvement in India's startup ecosystem beyond professional cricket. His portfolio spans businesses working in financial technology, electric mobility, drone manufacturing, digital entertainment and clean energy.

While the investment amounts and ownership details remain undisclosed for several companies, his involvement demonstrates how sports personalities are increasingly participating in India's entrepreneurial ecosystem.

As Dhoni transitions from an IPL player to a mentor, his business interests offer another perspective on his journey beyond the cricket field.

item.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 19, 2026)
item.description: YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, November 19, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.

Featured stories

Meet the women breaking barriers in deeptech, building technologies for tomorrow

On Women’s Entrepreneurship Day, we look at women founders pushing the boundaries of Indian deeptech, building frontier technologies, and opening new possibilities for innovation and entrepreneurship.

Read more

Anthropic raises $81.3B in IPO, surpasses SpaceX's record offering

Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic has raised $81.3 billion through its initial public offering (IPO), making it the largest stock market offering on record and surpassing Elon Musk-led space company SpaceX's $75 billion IPO. Anthropic priced its shares at $83 apiece, above the previously indicated range of $70-78 per share. The company is set to make its Nasdaq debut on Thursday, November 19, at a valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion.

Read more

Six Indian startups selected for Hub71's Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi

Six Indian startups have been selected for Hub71's Immersion Programme in Abu Dhabi, following the UAE-India Start-Up Series 2.0 finale in Bengaluru. Hub71, Abu Dhabi's global tech ecosystem, is the cross-border partner which will connect the startups with investors, corporate and government partners, regulators, and prospective customers.

Read more

Funding news

Style Union raises Rs 485 Cr to expand beyond southern India

Nexon Omniverse Limited, the parent company of value-fashion retailer Style Union, has raised Rs 485 crore in a Series E round led by Venturi Partners, a consumer-focused investment firm, and co-led by Elev8 Venture Partners, a growth-stage investor.

Read more

Quick service restaurant chain Boba Bhai raises $18M in Series B round

Boba Bhai, an Indian bubble tea and Korean street food brand, has raised $18 million in a Series B funding round with participation from Left Lane Capital and BIG Capital, alongside existing investors including Titan Capital.

Read more

InPrime Finserv raises Rs 101 Cr in Series B round led by FMO

InPrime Finserv, a tech-led NBFC, has raised Rs 101 crore in a Series B funding round led by FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank. This round also saw participation from existing investors Z47 and Pravega Ventures.

Read more

Disseqt AI raises $8M to build enterprise AI safeguards

Disseqt AI, a Dublin-headquartered AI assurance company with a significant presence in India, has raised $8 million in a round led by Gresham House Ventures, the growth equity arm of investment manager Gresham House.

Read more

VitusCare raises $3 million in Series B funding

VitusCare, a dialysis care provider, has raised $3 million in a Series B funding round led by Singapore-based healthcare growth equity firm Liberty Ridge Capital, with participation from HDFC Bank, Equentis, NAFA Capital Advisors, existing investors 1Crowd and 3i Partners, and angel investors. The company said its revenue has nearly tripled since its previous funding round in late 2024. Its network has expanded from 22 to over 60 dialysis centres across nine states and more than 50 cities.

VitusCare has treated over 35,000 patients and delivered 8 lakh dialysis sessions. It reported positive corporate EBITDA in FY26. It plans to expand to over 100 centres by FY27, besides investing in technology, AI-powered solutions and workforce training.

Other news

Intuit inaugurates new technology campus in Bengaluru

Global financial technology company Intuit has inaugurated its new Bengaluru office at Embassy Tech Village, strengthening its investment in India as a strategic hub for technology and AI innovation. The two-tower campus houses the company's second-largest engineering centre and nearly a quarter of its global technology talent is based in Bengaluru. Intuit has maintained a presence in the city since 2005. The new facility features collaborative workspaces, focus zones and locally inspired artwork and design.

The company said the campus would support the development of AI-powered products and financial technology solutions for customers worldwide. Alex Balazs, Chief Technology Officer, Intuit, said Bengaluru teams were central to building AI-driven experiences that help customers prosper.

CoinDCX-backed Digital Suraksha Network partners Karnataka government

Digital Suraksha Network (DSN), a non-profit platform focused on combating digital financial fraud, has signed an MoU with the Centre of Excellence for Cybersecurity (CySecK), an initiative of the Karnataka government. The partnership will strengthen cybersecurity awareness, skills development and industry collaboration across the state. The organisations plan to conduct Kannada-language cyber safety campaigns targeting one crore citizens by 2027. They will also provide training resources and mentorship to students, government officials and cybersecurity startups.

DSN was launched by CoinDCX's co-founders in March 2026. According to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, over 65.89 lakh financial fraud complaints were registered between 2021 and 2025, involving reported losses exceeding Rs 55,050 crore.

Zurich Insurance Group to expand Hyderabad GCC to 1,000 employees by 2028

Zurich Insurance Group plans to expand its India Capability Centre in Hyderabad to approximately 1,000 employees by mid-2028, strengthening its global technology, engineering, data and AI operations. The centre forms part of the insurer's global operating model, with teams in India working alongside colleagues across international markets.

Zurich plans to recruit specialists in cloud and platform engineering, data and AI, application development, cybersecurity and quality engineering. The company also intends to increase the centre's responsibility for end-to-end ownership of projects, from defining business requirements to developing and implementing solutions. Amit Kalra, Global Head of Zurich Capability Centres, will lead the development of additional leadership and decision-making capabilities in India.

Cognizant launches immersive learning centre in Chennai

Cognizant has unveiled the first phase of its Cognizant Immersive Learning Center at its Siruseri campus in Chennai, reinforcing its focus on developing technology and AI capabilities among employees. The facility is designed to provide associates with opportunities to explore emerging technologies, acquire new skills and prepare for changing business requirements.

The initiative forms part of the company's broader workforce transformation strategy as AI adoption reshapes technology services and enterprise operations. Rajesh Varrier, President – Global Operations and Chairman and Managing Director, Cognizant India, said the company's focus was on harnessing AI to transform businesses while developing the skills employees need to lead that transformation. The centre is expected to support continuous learning and innovation.

InMobi launches agentic AI advertising platform for businesses

InMobi has launched InMobi Accelerate, a self-service agentic AI advertising platform designed to plan, build, launch and measure campaigns across multiple advertising channels through a single dashboard.

Targeted at small and medium-sized businesses and advertising agencies, the platform uses seven specialised AI agents covering business analysis, audience strategy, media planning, copywriting, creative design, campaign launch and optimisation. It supports Google Ads, Meta Ads, Microsoft Advertising, TikTok Ads and ChatGPT Ads, among other platforms. Advertisers can approve campaign plans, budgets and creatives before launch and subsequently manage campaigns through plain-English instructions.

InMobi said the platform also provides a consolidated cross-channel view of advertising performance, helping businesses measure returns and optimise spending.

Pine Labs launches stablecoin-linked payment infrastructure platform

Pine Labs has launched Staq Web3 Orchestrator, a technology platform designed to connect stablecoin balances with conventional card payment infrastructure. The platform aims to simplify the development and operation of stablecoin-linked card programmes by bringing together regulated card issuance, payment processing and programme management. It is being deployed in a stablecoin-linked card programme, with Reap serving as the issuer and BIN sponsorship partner.

Pine Labs will manage the customer proposition, programme operations, technology stack and ecosystem integration, while Reap provides card-issuing infrastructure. The platform supports virtual and physical prepaid cards and online and offline payment experiences. The launch marks Pine Labs' expansion beyond traditional merchant payments into digital assets and mainstream payment infrastructure.

Cashify reports Rs 6.49 Cr net profit in FY26

Cashify has reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 6.49 crore for FY26, compared with a net loss of Rs 10.56 crore in the previous financial year. Revenue from operations increased 50% to Rs 1,641.19 crore, while consolidated EBITDA rose to Rs 22.7 crore from Rs 1.98 crore in FY25.

The recommerce platform attributed its performance to growth in smartphone buybacks, refurbishment and sales, alongside improved operating efficiencies. Employee costs declined to 9% of revenue from 10.5%, even as total expenses increased 45.7%. Cashify now plans to expand beyond smartphones into laptops, tablets, smartwatches, gaming consoles and audio devices, extending its buyback and refurbishment model across consumer electronics.

IBM partners Axis Max Life to strengthen database security

IBM has partnered with Axis Max Life Insurance to strengthen database security across the insurer's hybrid technology infrastructure. The collaboration aims to improve oversight of sensitive customer and financial information distributed across on-premises and cloud environments.

IBM Professional Services delivered the implementation, which is designed to enhance data protection and security controls while supporting the insurer's digital transformation initiatives. The project is expected to help Axis Max Life strengthen its ability to monitor and protect critical databases as it modernises its technology environment. Mukul Jain, Chief Technology Officer at Axis Max Life Insurance, said building a robust data security foundation was important as the company continued to strengthen its technology and digital capabilities.

Siemens launches AI engineering agent in India

Siemens has launched its Eigen Engineering Agent in India, an AI-powered solution designed to automate industrial engineering tasks. Unlike generic AI tools, the platform operates within engineering systems and understands project-specific context and constraints. It can support tasks such as programmable logic controller (PLC) coding, human-machine interface development and engineering documentation.

Siemens said the solution completes AI-powered workflows two to five times faster than manual alternatives, with up to 80% higher solution quality. Sixteen Indian customers are already using the platform, including Pelican Rotoflex and Z System Intelligent Controls. The technology was among more than 20 industrial AI innovations showcased at Siemens India's seventh Transform Innovation Day, attended by around 500 industry leaders.

BharatPe launches digital ledger to help merchants manage festive business

BharatPe has introduced Udhaar Khata, a digital ledger designed to help merchants manage customer credit, payment collections and bookkeeping during the festive business season. The platform digitises the traditional bahi-khata system, allowing businesses to record customer dues, set payment deadlines and track outstanding amounts through a dashboard. Merchants can also send payment reminders through WhatsApp and SMS, accompanied by UPI-enabled payment links.

The company said the solution aims to simplify bookkeeping and improve collections for small businesses handling higher transaction volumes during festive periods. Udhaar Khata is part of BharatPe's broader strategy to offer technology-led services beyond payment acceptance, including its recently introduced Agentic AI Suite.

Cloud.in joins OpenAI Partner Network as Select Partner

Cloud.in, the cloud, AI, quantum computing and cybersecurity business of Hostin Services, has been named an OpenAI Select Partner within the OpenAI Partner Network. The recognition will support its efforts to help enterprises develop, integrate and operationalise AI solutions.

The company plans to combine OpenAI capabilities with AWS Bedrock to offer model-agnostic enterprise AI services, focusing on security, governance, performance and cost considerations. Its areas of focus include enterprise AI transformation, intelligent automation and governed generative AI adoption. Cloud.in said it would pay particular attention to data governance, security and regulatory requirements for sectors such as BFSI and the public sector. The company has more than 27 years of experience in enterprise technology services.

Naxatra Labs appoints Naveen Deepak Veeramaneni as CPO

Indian deep-tech company Naxatra Labs has appointed Naveen Deepak Veeramaneni as its Chief Product Officer. He will lead the company's product development, engineering and manufacturing functions as it expands its electric motor and propulsion technology portfolio. Naveen brings experience in electric motor engineering and powertrain development, having spent nearly five years at Ather Energy, where he led motor engineering and subsequently the E-Powertrain team. At Naxatra Labs, he will focus on executing the product roadmap, strengthening design and development processes and improving integration between engineering and manufacturing.

Bank of India joins government's Bharatkosh non-tax receipt portal

Bank of India has announced its association with the Government of India's Non-Tax Receipt Portal (NTRP), also known as Bharatkosh, as an acquiring bank and payment gateway provider. The association will facilitate the collection of non-tax revenues through the government's integrated online platform. The arrangement is aimed at supporting digital payment transactions and providing users with an additional banking channel for making payments through the portal.

Bharatkosh enables the collection of various government non-tax receipts through an online mechanism. Bank of India's participation expands its role in digital payment infrastructure for government services and supports the government's efforts to make revenue collection more accessible and efficient.

Nupur Recyclers reports record Q2 FY27 performance

Nupur Recyclers reported its strongest-ever quarterly performance in Q2 FY27, with consolidated revenue rising 124.86% year-on-year to Rs 116.21 crore. EBITDA increased 148.48% to Rs 15.73 crore, while profit after tax grew 103.06% to Rs 8.80 crore. For the first half of FY27, revenue increased 90.27% to Rs 199.24 crore, EBITDA rose 130.34% to Rs 28.59 crore and PAT grew 93.19% to Rs 16.18 crore.

The company attributed the performance to improved production and capacity utilisation across its manufacturing and processing operations. Nupur Recyclers, which operates in ferrous and non-ferrous metal scrap processing, plans to strengthen capacity, improve operational efficiency and diversify across the recycling value chain.

Visage Lines appoints Vinod Nambiar as senior operating partner

Visage Lines, the parent company of Bombay Shaving Company, Bombae, The Mom's Co, rE and 100 Days, has appointed Vinod Nambiar as senior operating partner. Nambiar brings over three decades of experience in consumer businesses, brand building, retail and business transformation, including leadership roles at Hindustan Unilever and Colgate-Palmolive. He will work with the leadership team on manufacturing, product development, design and engineering, besides supporting the company's next phase of growth.

Indeed integrates employer services across Glassdoor and Indeed

Indeed has begun rolling out a unified login for employers across its job platform and Glassdoor, aiming to simplify recruitment and employer branding. The integration will allow businesses to manage their employer presence through a single account, access job listings across both platforms and use Indeed Smart Sourcing to identify candidates.

The companies will continue operating their respective websites independently. Job seekers will also be able to move between the platforms using one login, with shared information helping personalise their experience. Glassdoor reviews and conversations posted anonymously will remain unlinked to users' profiles. The development follows Glassdoor becoming part of Indeed earlier this year, as the companies seek to combine workplace insights with recruitment capabilities.

Apex Opinion launches independent medical advisory platform in India

US-based health technology company Krivox has launched Apex Opinion, an independent medical advisory platform for patients and families in India seeking specialist second opinions. Founded by Dr Saurabh Sanon, the platform connects patients with US board-certified specialists across medical disciplines. Patients can securely submit medical records and diagnostic reports for review and receive written second opinions, video consultations or multidisciplinary assessments through specialised panels. These include Heart Teams and Solid Tumor Boards.

Each opinion is signed by the reviewing physician, with a target turnaround time of seven business days after receiving complete medical records. Apex Opinion is accessible through its website and mobile applications. The company also plans to establish partnerships with hospitals and clinics in India.

Straive expands Microsoft partnership with 700-plus AI accelerators

Straive is deepening its partnership with Microsoft to help enterprises accelerate AI adoption and deployment. The company showcased its capabilities at Microsoft Ignite 2026, highlighting a portfolio of more than 700 data, analytics and AI solution accelerators. Its agent library brings together reusable workflows, AI agents and specialised tools designed to help businesses move beyond experimentation towards enterprise-wide implementation. Straive said customer-specific proofs of concept could be developed using customer data within seven to 14 days. The company recently achieved Microsoft's AI Platform specialisation and works across its Data and AI, Digital and Application Innovation, and Azure Infrastructure portfolios.

Hexnode adds native IT asset management to UEM platform

Hexnode has introduced native IT Asset Management (ITAM) within its Unified Endpoint Management platform, expanding its capabilities beyond enrolled devices to cover the broader workplace equipment lifecycle. The new functionality allows organisations to track laptops, monitors, accessories, furniture and other assets, alongside their assignments, purchase details, warranties and depreciation. It also includes QR-based physical audits and checkout records to help businesses manage equipment allocation and recovery.

The company has additionally introduced dedicated shared-device policies for Android and remote BIOS management for supported Windows PCs. The IT asset management capability is available to customers on Hexnode UEM's Enterprise plan and above, helping IT teams consolidate asset tracking and endpoint management.

Truecaller partners Bolna to bring transparency to enterprise voice AI calls

Truecaller has partnered with Indian voice AI platform Bolna to bring greater transparency and trust to AI-powered enterprise calls. The integration will allow Bolna's enterprise customers to use Truecaller for Business features without changing how their AI agents are developed. Businesses can display their name and logo during calls, provide personalised information about the purpose of each call and identify calls as AI-assisted.

The partnership also introduces post-call features that allow recipients to schedule callbacks when calls are missed or unanswered. The companies said the integration would benefit enterprises using voice AI for collections, renewals, KYC follow-ups and customer service. Bolna will manage conversations, while Truecaller will provide identity and contextual information.

Aurionpro secures additional order worth nearly Rs 100 crore

Aurionpro Solutions has secured an additional order worth nearly Rs 100 crore from a global hyperscaler for data centre infrastructure solutions. With the latest order, the aggregate value of engagements with the customer has exceeded Rs 400 crore, reflecting the expanding relationship between the two companies. The project is expected to strengthen Aurionpro's position in the data centre infrastructure segment as demand for AI-ready computing facilities accelerates. The company provides enterprise technology and data centre solutions, with capabilities spanning infrastructure, engineering and digital transformation.

Bhaskar Bhattacharya, Executive Vice-President and Head of Enterprise Business at Aurionpro, said the company appreciated the customer's continued confidence as it expanded its presence in the growing data centre market.

Mitra FMCG, Tanvi Foods announce Rs 600-crore strategic integration

Mitra FMCG and BSE-listed Tanvi Foods (India) have announced a strategic integration valued at ₹600 crore, aimed at strengthening their food processing, sourcing, procurement and distribution capabilities. The integration, exclusively advised by Bestvantage Investments, is expected to support expansion across domestic and international markets. The partnership will help Mitra leverage Tanvi Foods' export presence to enter high-value markets, including the US, UK and UAE. Mitra's distribution network will support Tanvi Foods' expansion in Northern India, while Tanvi Foods will help Mitra strengthen its presence in Southern India, particularly in household essentials. The arrangement will also provide Tanvi Foods access to raw materials such as flour, maida and edible oils through Mitra's sourcing ecosystem, improving procurement efficiencies and supply-chain operations.

UpTik crosses Rs 100 crore in cumulative investments

UpTik, an invoice financing startup, has crossed Rs 100 crore in cumulative investments. The platform recorded approximately Rs 21 crore in investments during FY26, followed by Rs 79 crore between April and October 2026. Notably, October alone contributed Rs 21.38 crore in investments, exceeding the platform's entire investment volume for the previous financial year.

Alongside this growth, UpTik has maintained an investor retention rate of 80%+, indicating sustained participation and confidence among its investor base. Founded with the aim of connecting investors with businesses seeking working capital, UpTik operates in the invoice financing space, enabling investors to participate in financing business invoices while helping enterprises address cash flow requirements.

OVH Group unveils 55 new cloud and AI products

The OVH Group has unveiled 55 new products across cloud and artificial intelligence at its OVHcloud AI Summit, marking an acceleration of its AI strategy. The offerings span infrastructure, orchestration, inference and AI-augmented platform-as-a-service solutions. The company is expanding its cloud portfolio with NVIDIA RTX 6000 Pro, Blackwell B300 and Rubin R200 GPUs, alongside new virtual private cloud networking services. Its AI portfolio includes AI Fabric, serverless computing, AI Endpoints and enterprise-focused AI Agents and AI Search services. Through a partnership with Gladia, OVHcloud is also extending speech transcription and voice generation capabilities across more than 100 languages. The services will be available across public cloud, private cloud and on-premises deployment models, supported by three dedicated AI research laboratories.

Taboola completes acquisition of digital advertising firm Dianomi

Global performance advertising company Taboola has completed its acquisition of Dianomi, a digital advertising services provider focused on premium business, finance and lifestyle publishers. The acquisition strengthens Taboola's ability to offer specialised financial advertising solutions through its Realize performance advertising platform, which uses proprietary publisher inventory, first-party data and artificial intelligence. Dianomi connects leading advertisers, including with audiences across premium publishers. With a network of more than 600 advertisers and publishers, the acquisition is expected to expand Taboola's reach among high-value business and finance audiences.

Scalefusion wins Platinum award at 2026 MarCom Awards

Unified endpoint management platform Scalefusion has won the Platinum Level distinction at the 2026 MarCom Awards for its brand film, “One Platform. One Agent.
